title: A note about the next lesson
summary: Short heads-up that the newest version of the superheroes npm package changed its API, so the code in the next lesson must use a named import instead of the default import.

concepts.heading: API change in the superheroes package
points: Installing the current release of superheroes gives a package that exposes a named export, randomSuperhero, rather than a default export object with a random method.
Old pattern: default-import the package, then call its random() method. New pattern: named-import randomSuperhero and call it directly.

(Extra) This is the general ESM distinction: a default import takes whatever the module exports as default, while a named import in braces must match an exported name exactly. When a package updates, a lecture's import line can break even though the logic is the same.
(Extra) Importing with the ES module syntax requires "type": "module" in package.json (or a .mjs extension) when running under Node.

code_examples.caption: Updated usage for the current superheroes package
Older usage the video shows (superheroes v3 default export; fails with v4)
code_examples.code:
import superheroes from "superheroes";
const name = superheroes.random();

pitfalls: Copying the default-import line shown in the next video fails with the latest package version: Node throws a SyntaxError saying the module does not provide an export named 'default'.
Mixing up default and named imports produces errors such as a missing export.
